FLORA AND FAUNA

# FRINGING REEF (OFF FA'ASOUGA POINT)

--- SENTENCE 6619 ---
The fringing reef extends about 400 feet (120 m) offshore northwest of Fa'asouga Point.

--- SENTENCE 6620 ---
A nearshore channel of sand, rubble, and basalt boulders, 50 to 100 feet (15 to 30 m) wide, parallels the base of the beach.

--- SENTENCE 6621 ---
Near the point, the channel narrows to 10 to 30 feet (3 to 9 m).

--- SENTENCE 6622 ---
Beyond 100 feet (30 m) from shore, the channel mergds with consolidated limestone along the inner margin of the reef flat.

--- SENTENCE 6623 ---
Depth in the channel varies from 1 to 3 feet (0.3 to 1.0 m) (ASCRI-T2B1).

--- SENTENCE 6624 ---
From 100 to 275 feet (30 to 85 m) offshore there is a middle reef area with extensive Acropora thickets separated by areas of sand, rubble, and boulders.

--- SENTENCE 6625 ---
Depth varies from 6 to 24 inches (15 to 60 cm) (ASCRI-T2B2).

--- SENTENCE 6626 ---
The outer reef flat extends from 275 feet (85 m) seaward to the reef margin as a generally shallow limestone platform containing several exposures of basalt rocks (ASCRI-T2B3).

--- SENTENCE 6627 ---
The reef flat off Fa'asouga Point is very shallow (59).

--- SENTENCE 6628 ---
# FRINGING REEF (OFF FUSI)

--- SENTENCE 6629 ---
The fringing reef is about 350 feet (75 m) wide off Fusi Depth varies from 1 to 4 feet (0.3 to 1.2 m) at mean sea level.

--- SENTENCE 6630 ---
A nearshore depression extends seaward about 100 to 150 feet (30 to 46 m) from the base of the beach at Fusi.

--- SENTENCE 6631 ---
Limestone rubble and small boulders at the base of the beach grade to sand on the floor of the depression.

--- SENTENCE 6632 ---
The reef flat is a pavement of consolidated limestone partially exposed at low tide.

--- SENTENCE 6633 ---
inshore portion of the reef flat has numerous channels and large, deep pools containing sand, limestone rubble and small boulders.

--- SENTENCE 6634 ---
The middle reef flat, about 200 feet (60 m) offshore, slightly as a low, smooth platform of consolidated limestone.

--- SENTENCE 6635 ---
Depressions and scattered limestone rubble and boulders characterize the outer reef flat.

--- SENTENCE 6636 ---
The reef margin exhibits spur-and-groove development, with surge channels penetrating 30 to 50 feet (9 to 15 m) shoreward between limestone ridges or buttresses.

--- SENTENCE 6637 ---
slopes gradually seaward from the serrated reef margin.

--- SENTENCE 6638 ---
over 30 feet (9 m), the reef front drops to a gently-sloping bottom of limestone rubble and boulders (59).

--- SENTENCE 6639 ---
A small boat harbor is under construction on the reef flat northwest of Matavai Point.

--- SENTENCE 6640 ---
A 16-foot (5 m) deep entrance channel cuts across the reef to deep water (49).

#### MARSHLANDS

The marshlands behind Ta'u Village were probably once extensively cultivated.

--- SENTENCE 6641 ---
Vegetation is dense and appears to be reverting to a more natural condition.

--- SENTENCE 6642 ---
Dominant plant species are Ludwigia octovalvis (la'avai), Rhynchospora corymbosa (selesele), Eleocharis dulcis ('utu'utu), and, in areas of bare soil, large clumps of Acrostichum aureum (sa'ato).

--- SENTENCE 6643 ---
Hibiscus (fau) forms dense thickets on higher ground in places around the margin of the marsh (70;77).

--- SENTENCE 6648 ---
FRINGING REEF (OFF FA'ASOUGA POINT)

--- SENTENCE 6649 ---
Live coral covers about 5% of the sandy inshore areas northwest of Fa'asouga Point.

--- SENTENCE 6650 ---
Pavona decussata and Porites microatolls are most common.

--- SENTENCE 6651 ---
Numerous sea cucumbers (Holothuria hilla, H. cinerascens, H. difficilis, H. pervicax, and Stichopus chloronotus) occur under rocks and elsewhere.

--- SENTENCE 6652 ---
Algae present include a blue-green species (ASCRI-T2B1).

--- SENTENCE 6653 ---
Coral cover of up to 85% on the middle reef flat consists almost entirely of <u>Acropora</u> aspera thickets.

--- SENTENCE 6654 ---
The sea cucumber, <u>Holothuria difficilis</u>, is common in sandy areas (ASCRI-T2B2).

--- SENTENCE 6655 ---
Coral cover is about 10% on the outer reef flat.

--- SENTENCE 6656 ---
A total of 35 coral species representing 16 genera are present on the reefs off the Ta'u Village complex.

--- SENTENCE 6657 ---
Encrusting coralline algae and the fleshy, <u>Dictyosphaeria versluysii</u> are the most common algae.

--- SENTENCE 6658 ---
The sea cucumber, <u>Stichopus chloronotus</u>, is conspicuous (ASCRI-T2B3).

--- SENTENCE 6659 ---
The reef off Fa'asouga Point harbors a diverse fish assemblage of at least 45 species.

--- SENTENCE 6660 ---
The fish fauna of the inner reef flat is similar to that of reefs fringing the villages of Luma and Si'ufaga.

--- SENTENCE 6661 ---
Dominant species are the damselfishes, Glyphidodontops glaucus, G. leucopomus, Stegastes albofasciatus, and Abudefduf septemfasciatus, the wrasses, Halichoeres margarataceus and H. trimaculatus, and the surgeonfish, Acanthurus triostegus.

--- SENTENCE 6662 ---
An Acropora thicket in deeper water offshore provides abundant cover for fishes, where the composition of the assemblage is somewhat different than over the reef flat.

--- SENTENCE 6663 ---
Most abundant here are the damselfishes, Stegastes albofasciatus, S. nigricans, and Glyphidodontops cyanea, the wrasses, Thalassoma hardwickei and Gomphosus varius, juvenile parrotfish, Scarus spp., the surgeonfish, Acanthurus triostegus, and the butterflyfish, Chaetodon citrinellus (ASCRI-T2F2).

--- SENTENCE 6664 ---
FRINGING REEF (OFF FUSI)

--- SENTENCE 6665 ---
Although much of the reef flat fronting Fusi may be exposed at low tide, numerous depressions in the reef flat which remain submerged at depths of 1 to 5 feet (0.3 to 1.5 m) contain extensive coral and algae assemblages.

--- SENTENCE 6666 ---
Larger coral colonies occur in the pools compared with those on the shallow reef surface.

--- SENTENCE 6667 ---
Coral colonies appear healthy, and little dead coral is evident.

--- SENTENCE 6668 ---
A few corals grow on hard surfaces in the predominantly sand-bottom depression paralleling the shore.

--- SENTENCE 6669 ---
Scattered hydrozoans grow in small clumps over the reef flat.

--- SENTENCE 6670 ---
Cowries are present on the surface of the reef flat.

--- SENTENCE 6671 ---
At low tide, fishes are restricted to pools in the reef flat.

--- SENTENCE 6672 ---
Gobies, wrasses, and damselfishes are most common.

--- SENTENCE 6673 ---
At high tide, other fishes forage over the entire reef flat.

--- SENTENCE 6674 ---
Coral development is low in the narrow channel around Matavai and Vaitele Points.

diverse near the seaward opening of this channel.

--- SENTENCE 6681 ---
Coralline algae and burrowing sea urchins are conspicuous at the reef margin.

--- SENTENCE 6682 ---
The reef front harbors diverse fish and coral life.

--- SENTENCE 6683 ---
Scattered clumps of live coral and algae cover limestone debris over 30 feet (9 m) deep at the base of the reef front (59).

--- SENTENCE 6684 ---
# COAST BETWEEN VAITELE POINT AND SI'UFA'ALELE POINT

# FRINGING REEF

Longshore currents have scoured a small, narrow channel in the inner reef around Matavai and Vaitele Points.

--- SENTENCE 6685 ---
The channel attains a depth of 5 feet (1.5 m).

--- SENTENCE 6686 ---
A freshwater spring issues below sea level at Matavai Point.

--- SENTENCE 6687 ---
The 4-foot (1.2 m) deep channel around Matavai Point exposes consolidated limestone breccia abutting a vertical cliff of basalt (59).

--- SENTENCE 6688 ---
# FAGA COVE

A pocket beach of calcareous sand and rubble occupies the head of Faga Cove.

--- SENTENCE 6689 ---
The foreshore is 30 to 40 feet (9 to 12 m) wide.

--- SENTENCE 6690 ---
Beachrock is exposed along shore.

--- SENTENCE 6691 ---
The reef flat fringing Faga Cove is 150 feet (46 m) wide (49) and depauperate of marine fauna.

--- SENTENCE 6692 ---
A channel was blasted through the reef by the U.S. Navy after World War II (59).

--- SENTENCE 6693 ---
# COASTAL ZONE

A small strip of coastal forest dominated by Barringtonia asiatica (futu) inland of Matavia and Vaitele Points has escaped human alteration.

--- SENTENCE 6694 ---
This forest is considered worthy of preservation (70).

--- SENTENCE 6695 ---
The fruitbat or flying fox (pe'a; <u>Pteropus samoensis</u>) roosts in several localities on Ta'u, most notably in the trees on plantation land above Fagamalo Cove (15).

--- SENTENCE 6696 ---
# TA'U BOAT HARBOR

tion near Matavai Point has caused some soil erosion problems.

--- SENTENCE 6697 ---
At an inland quarry site, the drainage pattern feeding the Fusi wetland has reportedly been altered, eliminating a portion of the marsh.

--- SENTENCE 6698 ---
Soil erosion from a quarry site and temporary road along the shore of Fagamalo Cove has reportedly caused siltation of the beach and nearshore areas (39).

--- SENTENCE 6699 ---
# OFFSHORE (FAGAMALO COVE TO SI'UFA'ALELE POINT)

--- SENTENCE 6700 ---
The reef flat and deeper waters beyond the reef edge extending southward from Fagamalo Cove to Si'ufa'alele Point are frequently used for fishing.

--- SENTENCE 6701 ---
Fishing methods and catches are similar to those off Faleasao and Ta'u (20).

--- SENTENCE 6702 ---
(See FALEASAO / USE CONSIDERATIONS).

PHYSIOGRAPHY

# COAST BETWEEN SI'UFA'ALELE POINT AND SIU POINT (SOUTH COAST)

#

--- SENTENCE 6706 ---
COASTAL ZONE

The blue-gray noddy (<u>Procelsterna cerulea</u>), an uncommon resident seabird, nests near Fatatele Point on the southern coast of Ta'u.

--- SENTENCE 6707 ---
Large colonies of the common brown noddy (<u>Anous stolidus pileatus</u>) nest along the south coast from Papaotoma Point east to Ulufala Point.

--- SENTENCE 6708 ---
Small colonies are also found along the entire north, east, and west coasts of Ta'u.

--- SENTENCE 6709 ---
A major colony of the black noddy (<u>Anous tenuirostris minutus</u>), an uncommon resident seabird, nests on the isolated south coast of the island from Lavania Cove to Ulufala Point.

--- SENTENCE 6710 ---
A large colony of the common white tern (<u>Gygis alba pacifica</u>) nests in the same area (15).

--- SENTENCE 6711 ---
The fruitbat or flying fox (pe'a; <u>Pteropus samoensis</u>) roosts in several localities on Ta'u, most notably in the lowland rain forest above Papaotoma Point (15).

--- SENTENCE 6712 ---
# LAVANIA COVE

A large cave located just above the water's edge at Lavania Cove was known to be a major roosting site for white-rumped swiftlets (pe'ape'a; Collocalia spodiopygia spodiopygia), and sheath-tailed bats (pe'ape'avai; Emballonura semicaudata) until the early 1970's.

--- SENTENCE 6713 ---
The entire cave entrance has fallen in, perhaps destroyed by an earthquake on December 1, 1975, and there is no evidence that either birds or bats can now penetrate the mass of rock rubble.

--- SENTENCE 6714 ---
The cave was presumably destroyed as a nesting site.

--- SENTENCE 6715 ---
Despite large populations, the swiftlet is considered threatened because of its restricted nesting habitat (deep in caves).

--- SENTENCE 6716 ---
At least one cave harboring the sheath-tailed bat undoubtedly exists on the cliffs above Lavania Cove, but the location is unknown (15).

--- SENTENCE 6717 ---
# SOUTHERN COAST

The southern coast of Ta'u from Lavania Cove to Ulufala Point has been recommended as a natural area preserve off limits to hunting and other disturbances (15).

--- SENTENCE 6718 ---
COAST BETWEEN SIU POINT AND PAPASAO POINT (EAST COAST)

# SHORELINE AND COASTAL PLAIN

Along the eastern coast of Ta'u, a wide plain of coral rubble merges inland with talus slopes at the base of a steep cliff (15).

--- SENTENCE 6719 ---
The eastern shoreline from Luama'a to Papasao Point is a steep beach consisting almost entirely of limestone rubble and scattered basalt cobbles, with small pockets of calcareous sand.

--- SENTENCE 6720 ---
Beachrock is exposed intermittently along the shoreline.

--- SENTENCE 6721 ---
Beach width is about 50 feet (15 m) (49; ASCRI-T3S1).

--- SENTENCE 6722 ---
The beach

slopes up to a foreshore berm about 4 feet (1.2 m) high

--- SENTENCE 6725 ---
and then to an upper berm about 6 feet (2 m) high.

--- SENTENCE 6726 ---
The distance from the high water line to the coastal road ranges from 30 to 45 feet (10 to 15 m) (ASCRI-T3S1).

--- SENTENCE 6727 ---
Two beach berms, a backshore berm and a higher storm berm are indicative of high wave energy.

--- SENTENCE 6728 ---
The beach is directly exposed to trade wind waves (49).

--- SENTENCE 6729 ---
Beachrock is exposed at and above sea level.

--- SENTENCE 6730 ---
A large amount of coral and eroded limestone rubble are embedded in beachrock platforms.

--- SENTENCE 6731 ---
The beach merges offshore with a generally consolidated and irregular limestone reef (ASCRI-T3S1).

--- SENTENCE 6732 ---
The fringing reef is less than 100 feet (30 m) wide (49).

--- SENTENCE 6733 ---
# SHORELINE

Encrusting coralline algae and Ralfsia sp. coat the surfaces of beachrock exposed along shore north of Saua.

--- SENTENCE 6734 ---
A few wave-washed corals (Acropora humilis, Goniastrea sp., and Astreopora sp.) occur along shore (ASCRI-T4S1).

--- SENTENCE 6735 ---
# SAUA-LUAMA'A COAST

The unimproved road ends south of Papasao Point, and access to the southern coast of Ta'u is by footpath (49).

--- SENTENCE 6736 ---
# OFFSHORE (SIU POINT TO PAPASAO POINT)

--- SENTENCE 6737 ---
The reef flat and deeper waters beyond the reef edge extending northward from Siu Point to near Papasao Point are fished frequently.

--- SENTENCE 6738 ---
Fishing methods and catches are similar to those off Faleasao and Ta'u (20).

--- SENTENCE 6739 ---
(See FALEASAO / USE CONSIDERATIONS).

--- SENTENCE 6740 ---
The Saua coast is scenic and sparsely populated.

--- SENTENCE 6741 ---
The area is infrequently visited by tourists who come to watch the sunrise.

--- SENTENCE 6742 ---
Villagers from Fitiuta use the area for net fishing.

--- SENTENCE 6743 ---
Wave surge ovdr an uneven limestone bottom offshore limits swimming along the wave-exposed coast.

--- SENTENCE 6744 ---
On calm days, some areas may be suitable for wading.

--- SENTENCE 6745 ---
The sand beach along the entire coast is generally exposed to small waves.

--- SENTENCE 6746 ---
A small ava (channel) near Saua is exposed to waves and infrequently used to launch paopaos (ASCRI).

--- SENTENCE 6747 ---
The strip of coast from Tufu Point northward to Saua has been recommended as a natural area preserve off limits to hunting and other disturbances (15).

--- SENTENCE 6748 ---
# COAST BETWEEN PAPASAO POINT AND FITIUTA POINT

#### SHORELINE

--- SENTENCE 6749 ---
The shoreline below the village of Fitiuta consists of a basalt sea cliff and bench.

--- SENTENCE 6750 ---
The village is located well inland at an elevation ranging from 25 to 150 feet (7 to 46 m) (49).

#### FITIUTA VILLAGE

All Samoans acknowledge Manu'a as the source of Samoan traditions, with Fitiuta as the center.

--- SENTENCE 6755 ---
Fitiuta is mythologically the first village of Samoa and the home of the first of a line of Samoan chiefs equivalent to god-kings (30).

--- SENTENCE 6756 ---
The tomb of the last Tui'manu'a is located along the coast below Papatea in north Luma on the western coast of Ta'u (41).

--- SENTENCE 6757 ---
The only raised road in American Samoa is a wall-like path of stone extending inland through the village of Fitiuta from a boat landing.

--- SENTENCE 6758 ---
This road, believed to have been built by Samoans and Tongans, is a special road honoring the first of the line of god-kings endowed with supernatural powers.

--- SENTENCE 6759 ---
On this road, the god-king literally and symbolically stood above all (30).

--- SENTENCE 6760 ---
According to legend, there are two leaping places for souls of the deceased to depart to the afterworld near the village of Fitiuta.

--- SENTENCE 6761 ---
Pre-European petroglyphs are found along the coastline fronting Fituita Village (30).

--- SENTENCE 6762 ---
COAST BETWEEN FITIUTA POINT AND SI'ULAGI POINT (NORTH COAST)

#### MAIA BEACH

--- SENTENCE 6763 ---
A short section of sand beach fronts Maia along the north-eastern coast of Ta'u Island.

--- SENTENCE 6764 ---
The beach is bounded by basalt bluffs to the east and a boulder foreshore to the west.

--- SENTENCE 6765 ---
There is a gradation of beach material from basalt boulders at the eastern end, to limestone rubble in the center, to calcareous sand with a minor component of basalt at the western end.

--- SENTENCE 6766 ---
The beach is about 75 feet (23 m) wide, sloping up to the vegetation line at an elevation of 8 feet (2.5 m).

--- SENTENCE 6767 ---
The coastal road is situated close behind the vegetation line (49;ASCRI-T4S1).

--- SENTENCE 6768 ---
# FRINGING REEF (OFF MAIA)

--- SENTENCE 6769 ---
A fringing reef extends about 150 feet (45 m) offshore from Maia Beach.

--- SENTENCE 6770 ---
Average depth of the reef is one foot (0.3 m) (49).

--- SENTENCE 6771 ---
# NORTH COAST

A steep and narrow beach of basalt boulders forms the shoreline between Lepula and Avatele Cove.

--- SENTENCE 6772 ---
The boulder beach is interrupted by outcrops at points of land.

--- SENTENCE 6773 ---
A fringing reef ranging from 100 to 150 feet (30 to 45 m) in width protects the reach between Letula and Avatele Cove.

--- SENTENCE 6774 ---
The remainder of the northern coast lacks an offshore reef and is exposed directly to north and northwest swells and indirectly to trade wind waves.

--- SENTENCE 6775 ---
An unimproved road parallels the coast at the 12 to 15-foot (4 to 5 m) elevation between Lepula and Avatele Cove, but is separated from the foreshore by a steep, densely-vegetated bank (49).

MAP T4

USE CONSIDERATIONS

The coastline between Avatele Cove and Loto Point consists of a steep, narrow foreshore of basalt boulders backed by a cliff rising to the road at an elevation between 30 and 70 feet (10 to 20 m).

--- SENTENCE 6779 ---
Rock outcroppings at points of land interrupt the boulder foreshore.

--- SENTENCE 6780 ---
There is no fringing reef offshore.

--- SENTENCE 6781 ---
The backshore is heavily vegetated and the shoreline is almost inaccessible.

--- SENTENCE 6782 ---
From Loto Point west to Si'ulagi Point (MAP T1), the coastline consists of a sea cliff rising 200 to 300 feet (60 to 90 m).

--- SENTENCE 6783 ---
An unimproved road at the 300-foot (90 m) elevation parallels the coast (49).

--- SENTENCE 6784 ---
# ABANDONED VILLAGE

The oldest village in all of the Samoan Islands, traditionally and mythologically, was Faga, located about 3 miles (4.8 km) west of the present village of Fitiuta.

--- SENTENCE 6785 ---
Tradition states the Tui Manu'a was killed by invaders, and his blood desecrated the area so that the village had to be abandoned.

--- SENTENCE 6786 ---
The site, now densely vegetated, extends about a quarter of a mile (400 m) inland from the coast.

--- SENTENCE 6787 ---
Remains of numerous abandoned house platforms lie under brush (30).

--- SENTENCE 6788 ---
# SOLID WASTE DISPOSAL SITE

Disposal of solid waste on Ta'u presently occurs at a site on the north shore between Avatele and Au'auli coves.

--- SENTENCE 6789 ---
This site is on an extremely steep embankment adjacent to the ocean, and some of the waste is probably entering nearshore waters below (39).

--- SENTENCE 6790 ---
# OFFSHORE, MAIA TO AU'AULI COVE

The narrow reef and deeper waters offshore between Maia and Au'auli Cove are frequently used for fishing.

--- SENTENCE 6791 ---
Fishing methods and catches are similar to those off Faleasao and Ta'u (20).

--- SENTENCE 6792 ---
The narrow reef flat fronting Lepula, just west of Maia, is considered a "critical use reef area" supporting subsistence fishing by villagers (39).

--- SENTENCE 6793 ---
(See FALEASAO / USE CONSIDERATIONS).

--- SENTENCE 6794 ---
# MAIA BEACH AND OFFSHORE

The only sand beach near Fitiuta Village on the northeastern coast of Ta'u Island is at Maia.

--- SENTENCE 6795 ---
Access to the beach is from the adjacent paved coastal road.

--- SENTENCE 6796 ---
Several paopao's on the beach attest to fishing activity.

--- SENTENCE 6797 ---
Maia Beach is the major point of access for offshore fishing along the northeast coast.

--- SENTENCE 6798 ---
Net fishing occurs off Maia Beach.

--- SENTENCE 6799 ---
Turbulent waters nearshore usually make swimming and diving hazardous, except for the most experienced swimmer.

--- SENTENCE 6800 ---
Access to the open ocean is through a rip channel.

--- SENTENCE 6801 ---
Breakers across this channel limit safe exit and entry to infrequent periods of calm seas (ASCRI).
